sections.h2: What is it like to sell a house in Woodridge, Illinois?
sections.html:
Woodridge is a DuPage County village southwest of Chicago, just north of where I-55 meets Illinois Route 53, with small pieces of the village reaching into Will and Cook counties. A seller here is usually dealing with a post-war suburban house, townhome or condo in a place that grew in a single burst. The village was incorporated on August 24, 1959 with fewer than 500 residents, and its name comes from a wooded rise locally called "The Ridge" above the East Branch of the DuPage River.

Growth after incorporation was fast. The 1960 census counted 542 people, the 1970 census 11,028, and the 2020 census 34,158. A developer founded the village, and most of its homes, businesses and churches went up after the 1950s, so many houses are now old enough to need a new roof, windows, furnace or a rebuilt basement. That is the main reason owners here look at selling as-is.

Whether you list with an agent, sell on your own or take a cash offer, the same local paperwork applies. The sections below cover the Woodridge-specific steps, starting with who your neighbors are and which schools serve your address.

sections.h2: What do the numbers say about Woodridge homeowners?
sections.html:
Woodridge has about 13,300 households, and roughly two out of three homes are owner-occupied. The table lists the housing and income figures a buyer or appraiser is likely to look at first.

sections.h2: Which school district serves a Woodridge address?
sections.html:
It depends on the street. Woodridge has no high school of its own, and the village is split among several districts, so the district for your house can change the buyer pool. The village lists six districts on its school page: Center Cass 66, Community High School District 99, Lemont-Bromberek 113A, Lemont Township High School District 210, Naperville 203 and Woodridge School District 68.

  • Woodridge School District 68 runs six elementary schools (Edgewood, Willow Creek, Sipley, William F. Murphy, Meadowview and Goodrich) for grades K-6, plus Jefferson Junior High for grades 7 and 8.
  • Most high school students go to Downers Grove North or South in District 99.
  • Some southern Woodridge students are served by Lemont District 210 and attend Lemont High School.
  • Homes west of the DuPage River, in the Seven Bridges single-family area, attend Naperville District 203 schools.

Put the district name in your listing or your conversation with a cash buyer. It affects price expectations more than the age of the kitchen does.

sections.h2: What does a seller have to do at Woodridge Village Hall?
sections.html:
Anyone selling property in Woodridge has to buy a Real Estate Transfer Stamp from the village before the deed is recorded. The Finance Department page says stamps can take 60 minutes or longer to process and sometimes 24 hours or more, so allow time, or drop the paperwork off with a phone number and wait for a call.

Village Hall is at 5 Plaza Drive. The village does not accept stamp paperwork by email or fax, and original documents must be brought in or mailed with a self-addressed, postage-paid envelope. Questions go to 630-719-4909 or epay@woodridgeil.gov. Ask Village Hall for the current stamp amount before closing day, because it is a village charge and the closing agent will need the figure.

  • An exempt stamp is available when the transfer qualifies for an exemption under the state Transfer Tax Law.
  • A refund of the village transfer tax is available to someone who sold a primary residence in Woodridge and bought another residence in Woodridge.
  • Payment by check is converted to an electronic transfer, so the bank account can be debited the same day.
  • Mortgage lenders starting a foreclosure on a Woodridge home send a copy of the foreclosure notice to the Village Clerk at Village Hall.

At the county level, state law requires a transfer declaration signed by at least one seller and one buyer, or their attorneys or agents, when the deed is presented for recording or within three business days after the transfer, whichever is earlier (35 ILCS 200/31-25). The recorder will not accept the deed without it. Woodridge parcels can fall in DuPage, Will or Cook County, so confirm which recorder handles your parcel.

sections.h2: Do Woodridge permit and rental rules affect a sale?
sections.html:
Yes, in two ways: open work on the house and any rental use. Building permits are required for construction, alteration, repair, demolition or moving of any building in the village. The Community Development Department says it can issue some permits the same day, such as roofs, sewer repairs and water heaters. Other residential permits can take up to two weeks. Work must begin within three months and finish within one year of the permit.

If a house has an unfinished basement or addition, call Building Permits and Inspections at 630-719-4750 before you list, so a buyer does not inherit an open permit. Construction hours are limited: from September 1 to May 31, work stops at 7:00 p.m. on weekdays and Saturdays and runs 10:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. on Sundays, and in summer weekday work may run until 9:00 p.m.

The village also runs a Residential Rental Program. Owners of three or more multi-family units need an annual license by January 1 and take part in a yearly inspection. Owners of single-family rentals, or two or fewer multi-family units, register at no fee. Both groups complete a four-hour crime free housing seminar once, and the certificate goes with the registration. A buyer who plans to rent the house you sell will have to do this.

sections.h2: How do storms and flooding shape Woodridge houses?
sections.html:
Woodridge is in a humid continental climate, with record highs of 105 degrees in July 2005 and a record low of minus 26 in January 1985. Inspectors and buyers look at roofs, basements and drainage. On June 20, 2021, an EF-3 tornado struck just after 11 p.m., damaged 225 homes in Woodridge and neighboring suburbs and injured eight people who were taken to hospitals.

Storm repairs are one reason a roof or siding permit shows up in a house history. Another is stormwater: the village enforces the 2019 DuPage County Countywide Stormwater and Floodplain Ordinance as part of its building codes. If a basement has had water, say so on the disclosure form and keep the repair records.

The village has been named a Tree City by the Arbor Day Foundation, and more than 8,000 trees were counted on public property in a 1996 study. Mature street trees are part of the curb appeal, though a large limb over the roof is a fair item for a buyer to raise.

sections.h2: What are the ways to sell a house in Woodridge?
sections.html:
You can list it with an agent, sell it yourself, or accept a cash offer from a buyer who takes the house as it is. Each path ends the same way, with a transfer stamp, a recorded deed and a closing statement, so the real difference is timing and repairs.

  • Listing: best when the house is in good shape and you can wait for showings, inspection requests and a buyer's mortgage approval.
  • Selling yourself: saves a commission, but you handle disclosure forms, the contract and the village stamp yourself.
  • Cash offer: no mortgage underwriting and no repair negotiation, which suits inherited houses, houses with open permits, tenant problems or a deadline.

Whichever route you choose, compare the net proceeds, not the headline price. Add up repairs, carrying costs, the transfer stamp and the time you would spend waiting.

sections.h2: Who collects property tax on a Woodridge house?
sections.html:
The tax bill comes from the county where the parcel sits, so a Woodridge owner may deal with DuPage, Will or Cook County. Your bill lists the taxing districts, including the school district, park district and the fire protection district. Woodridge has no fire department of its own and is covered by the Lisle-Woodridge, Darien-Woodridge and Lemont fire districts, which each levy their own tax.

Ask the county treasurer for the status of every installment on your parcel before you sign a contract, and ask the closing agent how unpaid and prorated taxes will be handled. The village website has a Property and Tax Information section with pages on buying or selling a home and on municipal taxes.

faqs.q: Does the seller or the buyer deal with the Woodridge transfer stamp?
faqs.a: The seller needs to buy it, since the village states that anyone selling property in Woodridge must purchase a Real Estate Transfer Stamp. Your closing agent or attorney usually brings the paperwork to Village Hall at 5 Plaza Drive, because the village does not take stamp paperwork by email or fax.

faqs.q: Can I get my village transfer tax back if I stay in Woodridge?
faqs.a: Yes, in one situation. The village offers a refund when you sold your primary residence in Woodridge and then purchased another residence in Woodridge. Contact the Finance Department at 630-719-4909 to learn what documents it wants.

faqs.q: Which county records the deed for a Woodridge house?
faqs.a: Most of the village is in DuPage County, but small portions lie in Will and Cook counties. The county of your parcel decides which recorder takes the deed and which treasurer sends the tax bill, so check your parcel number with the closing agent.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit before I sell if I replaced a roof or water heater?
faqs.a: Yes, those jobs need a village permit, and the Community Development Department can issue some of them, including roofs and water heaters, the same day. If the work is already done without one, call 630-719-4750 and ask how to close it out before the buyer's inspection.

faqs.q: Does Woodridge regulate rental houses that I might sell to an investor?
faqs.a: Yes. Single-family rental owners register at no fee, and owners of three or more multi-family units hold an annual license with village inspections. Every owner or manager attends a crime free housing seminar once, so an investor buyer should plan for that step.
